search_objective: Identify authoritative sources reporting Legionnaires' disease cases, deaths, hospitalizations, and outbreak details in New York City during August 2025 (2025-08-01 to 2025-08-31), covering all target fields: confirmed/probable/suspected/unspecified cases, deaths, hospitalizations, dates, and sub-city locality.
search_reasoning: The task requires epidemiological data for a narrow one-month window (August 2025) in a specific city. The highest-value sources are: (1) NYC DOHMH (the primary local public health authority for Legionnaires' disease surveillance and outbreak response in NYC — historically very active on Legionella given the 2015 South Bronx outbreak and ongoing cooling tower regulations); (2) CDC/NNDSS for national notifiable disease surveillance that includes NYC data; (3) news media for outbreak-specific event coverage with case/death counts and borough-level locality; (4) ProMED or similar outbreak alert systems for rapid event reporting. The upstream planned queries use over-quoted, overly long strings that are unlikely to match real documents well (e.g., embedding the date range string "2025-08-01-2025-08-31" literally). This iteration replaces them with cleaner, more realistic queries optimized for each channel. Given the bounds of max 4 queries per iteration and max 10 total, this iteration uses all 4 slots on the highest-priority channels: official public health (NYC DOHMH / NYC.gov), CDC/national surveillance, news search, and a combined web search targeting ProMED/outbreak alert systems. Literature queries are deprioritized for iteration 1 because peer-reviewed publications for August 2025 events are extremely unlikely to exist yet.

query_batch.query: Legionnaires disease New York City August 2025 cases outbreak DOHMH
query_batch.query_rationale: Targets NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) and NYC.gov official communications. DOHMH is the primary surveillance and outbreak-response authority for Legionnaires' disease in NYC, issues health alerts, press releases, and publishes Epi Data briefs. Removing over-quoted strings and the literal date-range token improves recall against real document titles and metadata. 'August 2025' is the natural time anchor used in official documents.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: NYC DOHMH health alert, press release, Epi Data brief, or NYC.gov announcement with case counts and borough-level breakdown
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: nyc.gov domain, DOHMH authorship, official press release or health advisory language

query_batch.query: Legionnaires disease NYC 2025 outbreak cases deaths borough cooling tower
query_batch.query_rationale: News outlets (NY Times, NY Post, Gothamist, NBC New York, AP) are typically the fastest to report Legionnaires' disease outbreaks in NYC with case counts, death tolls, affected boroughs, and source building/cooling tower details. 'Cooling tower' is a key NYC-specific term because NYC Local Law 77 mandates cooling tower registration and Legionella testing — outbreak news almost always references this. This query is designed for a news search channel to surface August 2025 event coverage.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: News article from local NYC outlet or wire service reporting case counts, deaths, affected neighborhood or borough, and cooling tower or water source link
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Bylined news article from established outlet, quotes from DOHMH spokesperson or NYC Health Commissioner, specific case/death numbers

query_batch.query: Legionella legionellosis New York 2025 CDC NNDSS surveillance notifiable disease report
query_batch.query_rationale: CDC's National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System (NNDSS) and CDC's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR) are authoritative national-level sources that aggregate state and city-level Legionellosis case counts. CDC also publishes Legionella outbreak investigation reports. This query targets CDC.gov and related federal public health sources for any 2025 New York data. NNDSS weekly tables may include NYC-specific counts.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC NNDSS weekly table, MMWR report, or CDC outbreak investigation summary referencing New York or NYC Legionellosis counts in 2025
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain, NNDSS data table, MMWR citation, federal authorship

query_batch.query: Legionnaires disease New York City August 2025 ProMED outbreak alert cases
query_batch.query_rationale: ProMED (Program for Monitoring Emerging Diseases) and similar outbreak intelligence platforms (HealthMap, GOARN) aggregate and archive outbreak reports globally, including US city-level Legionnaires' disease events. ProMED posts are citable sources with evidence quotes, case counts, and dates. A general web search targeting ProMED alongside 'August 2025' maximizes the chance of surfacing any archived outbreak alert for the specific time window. This also catches any WHO or PAHO situation reports referencing NYC.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: ProMED post, HealthMap alert, or WHO/PAHO situation report referencing a Legionnaires' disease event in NYC in August 2025 with case or death counts
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: ProMED archive post with DON number or post ID, WHO disease outbreak news entry, or HealthMap event record

NYC.gov announcement referencing Legionnaires' disease outbreak investigation in August 2025

language_or_localization_reasoning: All queries are in English. New York City is an English-language jurisdiction; NYC DOHMH, CDC, and all major local news outlets publish exclusively in English for official disease surveillance communications. No localization to other languages is required. Disease terminology is standardized: 'Legionnaires' disease' is the common name used in press releases and news; 'Legionellosis' is the NNDSS/CDC notifiable disease term; 'Legionella' is the pathogen name used in cooling tower and environmental health contexts. All three are included across the query batch to maximize recall across source types.
trust_considerations: NYC DOHMH is the primary authoritative source for Legionnaires' disease in NYC; its press releases and health alerts are the gold standard for case counts and outbreak declarations
CDC NNDSS data may lag by weeks to months; August 2025 data may not yet be finalized or published at time of search
News articles may cite DOHMH figures but can introduce rounding, conflation of probable/confirmed, or premature counts — always prefer direct official source quotes
ProMED posts are citable but are secondary aggregators; they should be used to corroborate, not as primary case-count sources
Peer-reviewed literature for August 2025 events is extremely unlikely to exist yet and is deprioritized in iteration 1
Queries avoid over-quoting and literal date-range tokens (e.g., '2025-08-01-2025-08-31') that would fail to match real document text
stop_condition_hypothesis: Iteration 1 is sufficient if results return: at least one NYC DOHMH or NYC.gov official source with case counts for August 2025, at least one CDC or NNDSS reference, and at least one news article with borough-level detail. If these are absent or sparse, a second iteration should target borough-specific queries, NYC open data portals, and ProMED archives.
